newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sugar sector frets over prices, fuel.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sugar sector frets over prices, fuel.

text.p: Ukraine, awash with refined sugar produced from last year's beet harvest, is this year facing lower prices and fuel shortages at some of its sugar refineries, industry and trade sources said on Wednesday.
Olexsander Bohatarenyk, deputy head of the state sugar concern Ukrsukor, said 19 of Ukraine's 191 sugar refineries had stopped working due to fuel shortages and that wholesale prices had turned sour.
"Ukraine's sugar sector is facing ruin," he said.
"We are continuing to stick to our forecast for refined sugar output, but the sector is fast approaching financial catastrophe."

Ukraine expects to refine 2.8 million tonnes of white sugar from its 1996 beet harvest, far below last year's 3.49 million. So far, 1.3 million tonnes have been refined, compared with 1.9 million at this time last year.
With the sugar beet harvest days away from completion, Ukraine has forecast a low net beet output of 26 million tonnes, against 30 million in 1995.
"We can produce this quantity (the 1996 target) of refined sugar, but the question is, who will buy it," Bohatarenyk said, blaming a lack of government support and credit mechanisms for the sector.
He said a surplus of refined sugar from last year had caused domestic wholesale prices to drop to 700 hryvnia ($380) per tonne.
Ukrainians selling sugar by the kilo from plastic bags in the street are having trouble getting rid of supplies.
A Western trader said prices, including the cost of delivery to any Ukrainian border for export, had fallen to around $400 a tonne from $450-$460 a year ago.
"And those were bad prices last year," the trader said.
He said depressed prices had left refineries unable to purchase heavy fuel oil and diesel for operations and transport.
"The harvest is bad enough this year without this," he said. "The situation is much worse than last year."
Sources said the fuel oil crisis had particularly affected the Vinnytsia region east of Kiev, where three refineries had stopped working.
Agriculture Ministry statistics put sugar beet yields at 19.7 tonnes per hectare, far below last year's 22.3 tonnes.

The Western trader said he expected Ukraine to export one million tonnes to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan and Russia, despite the fact that Russia had a 10 percent value-added tax on Ukrainian shipments to counter what Moscow called dumping.
"Russia has 600,000-700,000 tonnes from last year in its warehouses, and lots of that is Ukrainian sugar," he said.
The Ukrainian government announced this year that it planned to privatise all but one of its 191 ageing sugar refineries, many of which were built in the last century.
Total rated refining capacity of five million tonnes a year has been eroded by obsolete equipment and technology.
